Can you study dentistry abroad without clearing NEET?

It was not long ago that the world was hit by a global pandemic and the need for more doctors, dentists and paramedics increased manifolds. The importance of and inclination towards studying dentistry as a field of Medical Science is as much as that of studying MBBS, if not more. Being a dentist not only brings a lot of repute but also is a crucial branch of Medical Science. To become a dentist in India, a student has to appear for NEET after passing the 12th standard.

The guide

This article covers everything you need to know about the exam, and also has answers to if you can study dentistry abroad without clearing NEET.

What is NEET?

NEET is the abbreviation for The National Eligibility Entrance Test which is the qualifying test for MBBS and BDS Programmes in Indian Medical and Dental Colleges. Conducted and looked over by the National Testing Agency, this test was formerly called the All India Pre-Medical Test (AIPMT). To conclude NEET is the gateway to entering the field of Medical Sciences and a good NEET Score is one to getting admission to a good medical school/college.

Modifications in requirements and its Impact.

Earlier, students willing to study BDS abroad were not obligated to sit in the NEET Examinations as some medical schools/colleges/universities granted admissions that were not based on NEET Scores. A student who aspired to study BDS from an Indian college was supposed to take a NEET Examination compulsorily.

But, as per the notice of the Dental Council of India, rolled out on September 5th, 2018, the eligibility criteria to pursue undergraduate dental courses abroad were made stringent by making NEET a compulsory test that had to be taken if a student were to become eligible to obtain “Eligibility Certificate” from the Dental Council of India (DCI) and practice dentistry.

    Impact of update on Aspirants

    Now that we know about the new mandates and requirements for getting admission to medical colleges/universities abroad, it seems to be harder than before to be able to enroll in a field that was never easy before and now has become even more difficult than ever!

    But, here are our two cents on the whole issue, and our advice on how to tackle it.

    First of all, the option of not appearing for NEET was desirable as it saved the students from facing disappointment in the form of a low score due to poor performance.

    Secondly, most students prefer studying in India itself since they are not aware of the benefits of studying dentistry abroad.
